drawdown_context: Price $39.22 on 2025-05-15, -41.1% from 52w-high $66.62. NOT yet delisted/distressed at cutoff (FMC remained in S&P 500/600 universe). Forward 1y return: -66.6% (worst-performing 'survivor' in the cohort). Re-scoring asks: was this collapse detectable at 2025-05-15 from the FY2024 10-K (filed 2025-02-28) + Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-01)?

rfm_tuples.R: 'We expect 2025 revenue will be in the range of approximately $4.15 billion to $4.35 billion, essentially flat at the midpoint versus 2024 ... [adj] EBITDA of $870 million to $950 million, an increase of 1 percent at the midpoint versus 2024 results.' (FY2024 10-K, 2025 Outlook). REAFFIRMED in Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-01) despite Q1 revenue -14% YoY.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: Q1 actuals as forward indicator. If full-year guidance is credible after a -14% Q1, the remaining 9 months need >+5% growth. Cross-check: regional/product trajectory vs guide.
rfm_tuples.M_source: FY24 10-K + Q1 2025 10-Q (pre-cutoff filing 2025-05-01) — internal claim consistency + arithmetic
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 revenue $791.4M vs $918.0M PY (-14%). NA -28%, Asia -24% (channel destocking), EMEA -11%; only LatAm +10%. Q1 adj EBITDA $119.7M vs $160.6M PY (-25%). To hit $4.25B midpoint, FY25 must produce $3.46B over Q2-Q4 = +5.2% vs PY Q2-Q4 of $3.29B. Q1 price decline of -9% (over half from cost-plus diamide contract adjustments) is structural, not transitory. Guide also reaffirmed despite $15-20M of NEW tariff costs flagged.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding: the FY25 guide is mathematically aggressive after Q1 collapsed -14%. Reaffirming flat-to-up guidance while diamide cost-plus pricing is structurally reset down (passing manufacturing-cost decreases through to partners) is the classic 'channel-inflation backstop' tell. Management is implicitly asserting H2 will snap back to growth — but channel destocking is multi-quarter and patent cliff is permanent. This is the kind of 'hold the line on FY guide' behavior that precedes guidance withdrawals.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On February 3, 2025, we entered into Amendment No. 3 to our Revolving Credit Facility to amend the maximum leverage ratio and minimum interest coverage ratio to provide additional financial flexibility given current market challenges. ... maximum leverage ratio is increased to 5.25 through the period ending September 30, 2025 and will incrementally step down ... ending at 3.75 for the quarter ended December 31, 2027.' (FY24 10-K Note 12).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm covenant amendment exists. Mode B: check whether amendment was NEEDED — was actual leverage already approaching the prior cap?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K disclosure + 8-K filed 2025-02-04 (Amendment 3) and 2025-02-11 (Amendment 4 — maturity extension to 2028); leverage math
rfm_tuples.M_value: Actual leverage at 12/31/2024 was 3.72x vs old covenant cap of 5.00x (74% utilized of the cap). Actual interest coverage was 3.90x vs old min 3.00x. Despite being IN compliance, FMC preemptively negotiated covenant relief raising max leverage to 5.25x and stepping back to 3.75x only by Q4 2027 — a 3-YEAR runway of relaxed terms. Followed 11 days later by maturity extension to June 2028 (Amendment 4). Short-term debt jumped from $337.4M (12/31/24) to $975.8M (3/31/25) per Q1 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding — this is the strongest pre-cutoff distress signal. FMC took covenant relief while still in compliance, indicating they expect leverage to BREACH 5.00x in 2025-2026 given their own forecasts. The 3-year step-down to 3.75x by Q4 2027 implies management privately models deleveraging will take that long. The simultaneous maturity extension signals refinancing risk anxiety. Short-term debt nearly tripling QoQ (Q4'24 to Q1'25) confirms working-capital stress is acute. Classic 'covenant relief before you need it' tell consistent with management knowing the next 4-6 quarters will be ugly.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Our core portfolio includes one of our two diamide-class molecules - Rynaxypyr (chlorantraniliprole) active, the world's leading insect control technology - with annual revenues of approximately $1.0 billion in 2024 ... we expect Rynaxypyr active to continue a steady growth trajectory notwithstanding the expiration of composition of matter patents covering Rynaxypyr active in certain countries which started in late 2022.' (FY24 10-K Item 1).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: Confirm the patent expiry schedule. Check whether 'steady growth trajectory' is consistent with multi-country composition-of-matter loss. Cross-check generic launches.
rfm_tuples.M_source: FY24 10-K patent disclosure (Item 1 + Risk Factors) + reading Q1 2025 10-Q for actual diamide revenue trajectory
rfm_tuples.M_value: Filing itself states: chlorantraniliprole patent 'expired in a number of countries in August 2022; this patent protection for composition will end in 2027 across all geographies.' Cyantraniliprole expiry 'starting in January 2024 ... expiring on a country-by-country basis at various dates through January 2029.' AND filing acknowledges: 'Generic competitors have, in some countries, registered and launched generic versions of our Rynaxypyr-based products.' Q1 2025: insecticide revenue $402.7M vs $501.3M PY = -20% YoY; total Asia -24%. Composition of matter patents covering FMC's $1B+ flagship product expire globally by 2027.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The patent cliff is fully disclosed in the filing itself (this is Mode A PASS — they didn't hide it). The framework finding is Mode B: 'steady growth trajectory' for a product losing composition-of-matter protection in its largest markets within 2 years, with generics already launched and Q1 insecticide revenue down -20%, is not credible. The pharma analog (post-LOE revenue declines of 70-90%) suggests $700M+ of Rynaxypyr revenue is at risk by 2027. Combined with C2 (covenant relief) this is the structural distress story.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On February 13, 2025 and February 14, 2025, two other purported FMC shareholders filed putative class action complaints ... captioned Mohammed v. FMC Corporation, et al. and Macomb County Employees' Retirement System ... [alleging] (1) that channel inventory management initiatives were not progressing as anticipated; (2) challenges arising from product pricing; and/or (3) the financial impact of cost-plus pricing arrangements with distributors.' (FY24 10-K Note 18).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: securities class-action existence check. Mode B: do the SPECIFIC ALLEGATIONS overlap with what management is still claiming in this same 10-K?
rfm_tuples.M_source: FY24 10-K Litigation note + cross-check vs current MD&A claims
rfm_tuples.M_value: Three separate securities class actions are now consolidated/pending: (1) original In re FMC Corporation Securities Litigation filed Nov 2023 (E.D. Pa.) alleging diminished patent protection and undisclosed generic competition in India/China/Brazil; (2) Mohammed Action filed Feb 13, 2025 — TWO WEEKS BEFORE this 10-K — alleging channel-inventory and cost-plus pricing misreps; (3) Macomb County Action filed Feb 14, 2025. Class period extends to Feb 4, 2025 (the bad-earnings day). The Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-01) confirms over half of Q1 revenue decline was from cost-plus contract resets — exactly what plaintiffs allege was concealed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding — this is the cleanest signal in the filing. Two brand-new class actions filed 2 weeks before the 10-K, with a class period running through Feb 4 2025, alleging the EXACT mechanisms that Q1's bad print confirms (cost-plus reset, channel inventory mismanagement). Plaintiffs are credibly pricing-in what management still calls 'current market challenges.' Three securities suits with overlapping fact patterns is a strong base-rate predictor of multi-year share underperformance and increased disclosure scrutiny.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On February 4, 2025, we released our results for the year ended December 31, 2024 as well as guidance for the first quarter of 2025 and full year 2025 and, our stock price declined significantly. We are evaluating whether this decline, if sustained, represents a triggering event and if an impairment test is required in connection with the preparation of the consolidated financial statements for the first quarter of 2025.' (FY24 10-K, Goodwill note + subsequent events).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: registered goodwill of $1,507M and intangibles of $2,360.7M. Was Q1 2025 10-Q test performed? Mode B: contrast voluntary disclosure of triggering-event risk against Q1 conclusion.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 10-K signaled triggering-event risk explicitly. Q1 2025 10-Q Note 4: 'There were no events or circumstances indicating that goodwill should be evaluated for impairment as of March 31, 2025.' Goodwill held flat at $1,515.1M ($8M FX uptick from $1,507M). Net intangibles $2,366.6M (held flat). Despite stock down ~40% from 52w high and Q1 revenue -14%, management chose to defer the impairment test.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Sequencing tell: management foreshadowed the triggering-event question in the FY24 10-K, then declined to acknowledge it in Q1 10-Q despite no fundamental improvement and a continued depressed stock price. Goodwill of $1.5B + intangibles of $2.4B = $3.9B (33% of total assets $11.8B). The 'kicked-can' on impairment combined with C2 (preemptive covenant relief) suggests management is delaying recognition of the rebasing now visible in cash flows. High likelihood of large non-cash impairment within 2-3 quarters.

rfm_tuples.R: Mode B: inventory dynamics. Q1 2025 10-Q balance sheet shows inventories grew from $1,201.6M (12/31/24) to $1,374.4M (3/31/25), a $172.8M build (+14% QoQ). Management explains: 'Changes in inventory reflect the higher inventory build required during 2025 to meet current year demand compared to the 2024 period.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: Verify whether inventory build is consistent with reaffirmed full-year guide, OR if it is producer-side accumulation while channel destocks.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025: inventory +$173M while revenue -14% YoY and customers explicitly 'prioritize holding lower than historical inventory' (per FY25 outlook language). Trade receivables held flat at $2,900M while sales declined — implies extended DSO. Short-term debt rose by $638M QoQ to $975.8M, partially funding the inventory + working capital. Q1 free cash flow not isolated, but full-year FCF guide $200M-$400M vs FY24 strong WC release.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding: producer-side inventory build during customer-side destocking is the canonical pre-impairment signal in agrochem. FMC is funding inventory growth with short-term debt while accounts receivable do not turn — DSO is extending. Either (a) they expect H2 demand to absorb the inventory (consistent with the reaffirmed guide but inconsistent with channel commentary), OR (b) inventory will be written down. Historical agrochem playbook (cf. CF Industries 2015, Mosaic 2015) is option (b).

rfm_tuples.R: Mode B: 'In connection with an amendment to the Company's credit agreement in November 2023, the Company agreed that it will not repurchase shares ... As part of the amendments entered into in February 2025 ... [continuing restrictions implied].' Dividend: per filing, FMC has paid dividends but no commentary on cut.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: capital-return restrictions in the credit agreement are an under-disclosed leverage signal. Verify in covenant text.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 10-K confirms: NO share repurchases in 2024 because Nov 2023 covenant amendment prohibited buybacks (except for equity-comp share withholding). Feb 2025 amendments continue these restrictions. Dividend per filing: still being paid but no expansion. Translates to: lenders required equity-cash-return suspension as condition of relief.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: capital-return restrictions in covenants are an under-priced signal that lenders view balance-sheet repair as priority. Combined with C2 (covenant relief Feb 2025), this means equity-holders are now subordinated to debt-repair for an indefinite period — and the dividend is at risk in any further amendment. The framework's Mode B 'what should be true if claim is true' check: management's strategy emphasizes investing-in-growth, but lenders have effectively locked them out of buybacks for the foreseeable future.

rfm_tuples.R: Auditor disclosure: KPMG signed unqualified opinion 2025-02-28 on FY2024 financials. No going-concern language; no critical-audit-matter escalation language flagged here.
rfm_tuples.M_source: auditor_change_tracker.query_auditor_changes(cik=0000037785, cutoff=2025-05-15) + visual scan of 10-K for 'going concern'
rfm_tuples.M_value: Auditor signal: CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE. 0 8-K Item 4.01 filings in 5y lookback (2020-05-16 to 2025-05-15). 0 Big-4 resignations. 0 disagreements. KPMG continuous. Going concern: 0 matches for 'going concern' in 10-K text (other than incidental ASC references). Auditor explicitly assumes continuity.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor and going-concern disclosure are CLEAN at the cutoff. This is a calibrated PASS — the framework correctly identifies that the most extreme distress markers (auditor resignation, GC language) are absent, even though every other claim flags structural stress. This is precisely the type of name where deterministic flags miss but R/f/M Mode B catches via covenant amendment + class action + diamide cliff + guide-vs-Q1 arithmetic.

rfm_tuples.R: Mode B: Insider behavior near earnings. Form 4 transactions in 365 days pre-cutoff.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: count buys (P) vs sells (S) by officers/directors; check timing near Feb 4 2025 earnings drop and covenant amendments.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Form 4 manual classification — SEC EDGAR filings 2024-05-15 to 2025-05-15
rfm_tuples.M_value: 92 Form 4 filings (365d). Codes: 107 A (RSU/RSA grants — May 2025 board-comp cycle), 23 F (tax withholding on vest), 4 M (option exercises tied to vest), 3 P (open-market PURCHASES), 4 S (open-market sells). The 3 buyers in early March 2025 (immediately after Feb 4 earnings collapse): Director Carol Anthony Davidson, incoming officer Ronaldo Pereira, and Chairman/CEO Pierre Brondeau — bought ON THE WAY DOWN at ~$40s. Only 4 small sales, primarily by mid-level officers in Jan 2025 (likely 10b5-1).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is a CONFOUNDING signal that warrants its own bucket. Insider buying by Chairman/CEO and a director immediately after the bad-print is consistent with 'we believe shares are oversold.' In the framework's typical short setups (heavy insider selling near capital events), this would PASS. Here we have the opposite — but ex-post the buyers were wrong (FMC dropped another -66% over the next 12 months). Net read: insider conviction does NOT save you from a structural patent cliff + channel reset + covenant pressure. Mark as UNVERIFIABLE because Mode B can't confidently flag absent the deterministic 'cluster sales near event' template. This is a known limitation.

rfm_tuples.R: Mode B: long-lived asset geographic mix shift. FY24 10-K table: long-lived assets in Asia DROPPED from $1,964.1M (12/31/2023) to $251.0M (12/31/2024), a -$1,713M decline; EMEA assets rose from $1,718.2M to $3,685.4M (+$1,967M). Footnote: 'In connection with our plans to establish a global technology and innovation center in Switzerland, we completed intra-entity transfers of certain intellectual property...'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: validate whether intra-entity IP transfer rationale is consistent with the magnitudes, and whether 'Switzerland IP migration' is a transfer-pricing/tax restructuring with associated risks.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Asia long-lived assets dropped 87% in one year. EMEA more than doubled. This is consistent with a Swiss IP-holding-company restructure (common in pharma/agchem for repatriation/tax optimization), but it concurrent with: (a) the India class-action allegations, (b) tariff exposure increasing $15-20M for 2025, and (c) Project Focus restructuring charges of $303M in 2024 ($375-425M cumulative). The Switzerland IP move also implies a meaningful one-time deferred-tax book/tax impact and increases the company's exposure to OECD Pillar 2 (acknowledged in Risk Factors).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the magnitude of the IP migration ($1.7B+ asset shift) is large relative to the brief 'global tech center' disclosure. Combined with Project Focus restructuring and emerging tariff/Pillar 2 exposure, FMC has multiple concurrent restructurings happening in 2024-2025. None individually trigger a red flag, but the aggregate complexity and tax-position-sensitivity raise the standard of evidence required to trust the financial-statement geometry — and reduce visibility into true underlying segment economics.

summary: At 2025-05-15, FMC's distress was DETECTABLE via R/f/M Mode B even though deterministic distress markers (auditor change, going-concern language) were clean. The strongest signals: (1) preemptive covenant relief Feb 3, 2025 raising max leverage 5.00→5.25 with a 3-year step-down — taken while actual leverage was only 3.72x, indicating management privately models worsening leverage; (2) two NEW securities class actions filed 2 weeks before the 10-K (Mohammed + Macomb County) alleging the EXACT cost-plus and channel-inventory mechanisms that Q1 2025 results then confirmed; (3) explicit diamide patent cliff (composition-of-matter expiry by 2027) with $1B+ Rynaxypyr franchise at risk and generics already launched; (4) reaffirmed FY25 guide despite Q1 -14% revenue and -25% adj. EBITDA — arithmetically requires H2 growth that contradicts management's own channel commentary; (5) self-disclosed goodwill triggering-event risk in 10-K, then deferred in Q1 10-Q despite no improvement. The confounding signal — Chairman/CEO + director open-market BUYS in early March — was ex-post wrong, illustrating that insider conviction does not override structural patent + channel + covenant stress. KEY ANSWER: yes, the framework would have flagged FMC one year earlier; deterministic-only screens (auditor, GC) would have missed.
